Siri AI is a major upgrade for the Apple assistant, now available on iOS 27. I've noticed a standout difference between it and other AI assistants, and it's a good one.

The all-new Siri in iOS 27 doesn't pretend to be human, unlike all other AI chatbots

Ever since the first beta of iOS 27 came out, I've been using Siri AI for nearly four months. Overall, it's met every expectation I had for it.

The new Siri is far more powerful than its predecessor, truly delivering on its original promise as a genuinely capable assistant on Apple devices.

That said, I do have to admit: if you need the most advanced, powerful AI tools out there, competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini may suit you better.

Having said that, after using Siri AI and then comparing it with those third-party tools, I noticed one key difference that has me clearly leaning toward Siri.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It doesn't go on at excessive length, nor does it mimic human-like personalities that draw you into forming personal relationships with it.

Siri is helpful, smart, and flexible, and it does what you ask it to do. But the way it responds makes clear that it's a tool, not a person. It frequently reminds you that it's an AI and may get things wrong. It also doesn't pretend to go on a date with you.

By contrast, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are all loaded with personality and opinions, showing more human-like qualities that feel, to me, less than authentic.

I expect some users enjoy this more 'personal' approach. But I'd much rather have an AI assistant stick to its job and stop pretending to be something it's not.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. I really appreciate that Apple understood this and built the all-new Siri on that foundation.

How 'human-like' do you think an AI assistant should be? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
